report.source_text: Treatment commenced, including high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine and rituximab, followed by radiotherapy (40 Gy total). Repeat MRI showed significant improvement in the central nervous system disease (figure 1G–I) and she also improved functionally, being discharged home without a package of care after previously needing 24 h nursing care. Ten months later, functional status had not deteriorated and neuropsychometric testing was equivalent to that done several months prior to commencement of treatment (ie, before significant further cognitive decline), however remaining below premorbid estimates. Importantly, her gait and mobility also improved dramatically as she went from being unable to walk unaided immediately prior to treatment, to walking independently, swimming twice weekly and using a cross-trainer regularly.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with primary central nervous system involvement
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old previously fit and well woman with no vascular risk factors presented with a 3-week history of subacute progressive amnestic syndrome, personality change, and emotional lability, followed by severe anxiety and insomnia. Neurological examination revealed universally brisk reflexes with downgoing plantar responses, marked language difficulty (expressive and receptive), ideational and ideomotor apraxia. Neuropsychometric testing showed marked impairments in memory, naming, literacy, and information processing speed with preserved executive function. Initial laboratory work on admission was normal (FBC, CRP, ESR, renal/liver function). Extensive serology and metabolic screening were negative (JCV, HIV 1/2, syphilis, amino acids, white cell enzymes, very long chain fatty acids, copper, coeliac screen, vitamin E, autoimmune antibodies, lactate, pyruvate, phytanic and glutaric acid). Brain MRI demonstrated extensive confluent T2-weighted hyperintensity diffusely throughout the cerebrum and brainstem without mass effect, contrast enhancement, or diffusion restriction. CSF analysis showed elevated protein (0.74 g/L), low glucose (3.2 mmol/L with serum 5.5), minimal cellularity (<1 WBC/mL), negative oligoclonal bands, and negative viral PCR, with cytology showing mild chronic inflammatory/reactive process. Brain biopsy revealed diffuse and nodular infiltration of cerebrum by large atypical lymphoid cells with nuclear pleomorphism, clusters around blood vessels, and diffuse spread into surrounding cortex. Further tests confirmed diffuse large B cell lymphoma. Bone marrow biopsy and PET/CT scan showed no evidence of lymphoma outside the central nervous system, confirming primary CNS lymphoma. Treatment commenced with high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine, and rituximab, followed by radiotherapy (40 Gy total). Repeat MRI showed significant improvement in CNS disease. Patient improved functionally, discharged home without nursing care after previously requiring 24-hour care. At 10-month follow-up, functional status had not deteriorated, neuropsychometric testing remained stable (though below premorbid estimates), and gait/mobility improved dramatically from being unable to walk unaided to walking independently and exercising regularly.

Extensive negative serology and metabolic screening: JCV, HIV 1/2, syphilis, amino acids, white cell enzymes, very long chain fatty acids, copper, coeliac screen, vitamin E, autoimmune antibodies, lactate, pyruvate, phytanic and glutaric acid
Brain MRI: extensive confluent T2-weighted hyperintensity diffusely throughout cerebrum and brainstem, no mass effect, no contrast enhancement, no diffusion restriction
CSF analysis: protein 0.74 g/L, glucose 3.2 mmol/L (serum 5.5), <1 WBC/mL, negative oligoclonal bands, negative viral PCR, cytology showing mild chronic inflammatory/reactive process

Brain biopsy histology: diffuse and nodular infiltration of cerebrum by large atypical lymphoid cells with nuclear pleomorphism, clusters around blood vessels, and diffuse spread into surrounding cortex
Further tests confirmed diffuse large B cell lymphoma
Bone marrow biopsy and PET/CT scan: no evidence of lymphoma outside the central nervous system (primary CNS lymphoma)
Treatment with high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine, rituximab, followed by radiotherapy (40 Gy total)
Repeat MRI showed significant improvement in CNS disease; patient improved functionally, discharged home without nursing care

At 10-month follow-up: functional status stable, neuropsychometric testing equivalent to pre-treatment baseline, gait/mobility improved from unable to walk unaided to independent walking and regular exercise
